item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00407","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C16","C17","C18"],"selected_candidate_label":"C16","confidence":0.82,"relationship_type":"structural_functional_template","rationale":"C16 plausibly supplied a material template: both memoranda reject special relief for a private contractor after losses arising under a valid Government contract, emphasize that the Government did not cause or bear responsibility for the loss, find no equitable basis for departing from the contractual allocation of risk, and warn against preferential or precedential relief. C17 and C18 contain similar contractual-risk and undesirable-precedent reasoning, but their factual and argumentative structures are less closely aligned with the child's concise sequence.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"fees ... had been properly paid pursuant to a valid contract","parent_excerpt":"losses sustained by it in performing its contract with the United States","explanation":"Both frame the proposed private relief as altering the financial result of an existing Government contract."},{"child_excerpt":"the Government was not responsible in any way for the failure to construct such housing","parent_excerpt":"the overriding causes of the losses which the contractor sustained were its own acts or omissions and the weather conditions it encountered","explanation":"Each assigns the operative loss to circumstances for which the Government was not responsible."},{"child_excerpt":"There is no proper basis upon which an exception can be made in this case.","parent_excerpt":"there is no basis for affording relief to the contractor on equitable grounds","explanation":"The memoranda use substantially parallel reasoning to deny an equitable exception to the contractual outcome."},{"child_excerpt":"Approval of this special relief bill would establish a highly undesirable precedent","parent_excerpt":"I perceive no merit in the claim for special treatment in this case","explanation":"Both conclude that preferential relief for this contractor is unwarranted and would undermine general treatment of comparable Government contractors."}]}
